title: Biblical Overlap Wave 16 — Circuits, Perimeters, Encampment & Threshold Motion
purpose: Refine the project's Circle/Orbit/Wheel/Spiral/Door vocabulary by distinguishing hostile surrounding, protective surrounding, ordered sacred perimeter, ritual circuit, throne-circumference and turning threshold-guard motion. Shape and recurrence do not carry one moral valence by themselves.
epistemic_rule: These are biblical structures compared with project geometry after the fact unless an earlier project-side biblical citation is independently documented. 'Around', 'encamp' or 'turning' is not automatically a literal Euclidean circle/orbit.

clusters.biblical_structure: human expelled from Garden → cherubim stationed at east → flaming sword described across translations as turning/whirling/flashing in every direction → Way to Tree of Life guarded
clusters.project_relation: This is unusually relevant to Door/threshold geometry because movement/turning occurs at the guarded access-point to Life itself. It joins boundary + guardian + directional motion + Way + Tree/Life in one verse.
clusters.boundary: Translations differ in how they render the sword's motion. Do not infer a literal orbital mechanism or project physics from the wording.

clusters.biblical_structure: prescribed repeated movement around a walled city → seventh-day sevenfold circuit → trumpet/shout → wall collapses → people move straight into city
clusters.project_relation: Creates a new recurrence class: a path may geometrically repeat around the same boundary yet culminate in a changed state. This differs from an endless Dog/vomit loop and from a spiral that changes radius/height continuously.
clusters.geometry_class: finite ritual circuit with terminal state transition
clusters.boundary: Joshua 6 is a conquest narrative culminating in destruction and killing. It must not be sanitized into a generic self-help metaphor; the geometric comparison concerns recurrence/boundary transition only.

clusters.biblical_structure: mountains surrounding Jerusalem become analogy for YHWH surrounding his people; angel of YHWH encamps around those who fear him and delivers them
clusters.project_relation: Direct counter-valence to Psalm 22 hostile encirclement. A perimeter can protect rather than imprison or attack.
clusters.boundary: The texts say surround/encamp; they do not specify geometric circularity in a mathematical sense.

clusters.biblical_structure: YHWH encamps at/around his House as guard → movement of threatening forces is restricted → oppressor no longer passes through → divine seeing/Eye language closes the verse
clusters.project_relation: A striking House + Guard + perimeter + passage-control + Eye cluster. It provides a positive protective form of boundary control and is particularly relevant to House/Eye/Gate project language.
clusters.boundary: The verse concerns protection from armies/oppressors in prophetic context. It does not authorize arbitrary modern gatekeeping or surveillance.

clusters.biblical_structure: tribes/households camp by standards and ancestral houses around the Tent of Meeting at a distance, oriented toward the sacred center
clusters.project_relation: Adds an ordered social-perimeter type: distinct groups remain differentiated while arranged around one sacred center. This is closer to organized radial participation than orbit/trap.
clusters.geometry_class: ordered differentiated perimeter around sacred center
clusters.boundary: The verse describes Israelite camp organization; it is not a proof of project North-Axis social order or literal radial geometry beyond the textual 'around/facing' arrangement.

clusters.biblical_structure: central heavenly throne → rainbow around throne → twenty-four thrones/elders around central throne → living creatures around/near throne → lamps/sea and continuous worship
clusters.project_relation: Shows circumference as ordered participation around a center rather than exclusion from it. Particularly relevant to throne/rainbow/wheel/eyes/centrality imagery.
clusters.boundary: Apocalyptic vision imagery should not be forced into a precise Euclidean diagram, planetary orbit or political hierarchy.

clusters.biblical_structure: Biblical surrounding/circling vocabulary appears with hostile, protective, organizational, sacred, liturgical and destructive/transformative functions.
clusters.project_relation: Circle/perimeter must be typed by actor, center, purpose, permeability, duration and outcome. The same abstract geometry can describe trap, protection, participation, worship or an action that terminates in boundary collapse.
clusters.boundary: This matrix is a project synthesis across distinct texts, not one biblical doctrine of geometry.

geometry_upgrade.closed_loop: repetition that returns to substantially the same state with no meaningful terminal change
geometry_upgrade.orbit: movement around a center while remaining outside/around it; may be stable, neutral or constrained depending on function
geometry_upgrade.protective_perimeter: surrounding whose function is guarding/delivering what is inside
geometry_upgrade.ordered_perimeter: differentiated participants arranged around a center without necessarily moving
geometry_upgrade.ritual_circuit: finite repeated route around a boundary whose prescribed completion terminates in a state transition
geometry_upgrade.throne_circumference: ordered relational placement around a sacred center
geometry_upgrade.dynamic_threshold_guard: moving/turning boundary defense whose function is access control
geometry_upgrade.wheel: recurrence organized around axle/axis; motion and center are coupled
geometry_upgrade.spiral: recurrence plus continuous displacement in radius/height/scale/description
geometry_upgrade.door: state-transition interface that can change which region/path is reachable

new_principles: Recurrence is not equivalent to stagnation. Ask whether the state after N cycles is unchanged, accumulated, displaced or terminally transformed.
Surrounding is not equivalent to hostility. Psalm 22, Psalm 34 and Psalm 125 supply opposite perimeter valences.
A perimeter is not necessarily an orbit: Numbers 2 is arranged encampment, not continuous movement.
A circuit is not necessarily a spiral: Joshua 6 repeats around one wall but changes state discretely at completion rather than continuously changing radius/height.
A sacred center can organize differentiated participants around itself without absorbing their identities, as Numbers 2 and Revelation 4 illustrate in different genres.

Boundary questions should track at least: who surrounds whom, what is centered, whether motion occurs, whether passage is allowed, what the boundary protects/restricts, and what changes after the cycle.
